Let \(A_n=\lambda n(7n+45)\) and \(B_n=\lambda n(n+3)\), since both sums have zero constant term.

Then
\[
a_n=A_n-A_{n-1}=\lambda(14n+38),\qquad b_n=B_n-B_{n-1}=\lambda(2n+2).
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{a_n}{b_n}=\frac{14n+38}{2n+2}=\frac{7n+19}{n+1}=7+\frac{12}{n+1}.
\]
For this to be an integer, \(n+1\mid 12\). Since \(n\) is positive,
\[
n+1\in\{2,3,4,6,12\},
\]
so
\[
n\in\{1,2,3,5,11\}.
\]
There are \(5\) such positive integers.

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
